# Native Whisper and Parakeet evidence

Reference app: unchanged Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`, using `onnx-asr` 0.12.0, CPU ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 and GPU ONNX Runtime 1.26.0. Imported application/resource files, including the GPU requirements, were checked against the release commit. Ten imported `onnx-asr` source/data files were checked against its size/SHA-verified wheel; the reference CPU library matches the independently extracted verified native library exactly. The released GPU installer ran in disposable storage with its unchanged hash-locked wheels. Collection helpers remain outside the maintained tree under ignored task scratch.

`released-frontends.json` and paired compressed PCM/features freeze 22 independent NumPy cases and all 2,017,792 feature values. They cover zero-length/silent audio, 1/159/160/161/319/320/511/512-frame boundaries, impulses, deterministic noise through the full 25-second block and the public English/Chinese clips used by [Qwen's examples](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/main/README.md). Files carry decompressed size/SHA checks. Native dimensions, valid lengths, masking and finite/NaN/infinite classification must match; finite feature values permit at most `1e-5` absolute difference. The explicitly observed maximum is `2.6226044e-6` for NeMo and `2.3841858e-7` for Whisper on this x86-64 machine. These bounds cover FFT/float arithmetic differences; they are not a transcript-quality metric. Short NeMo inputs deliberately retain the reference normalization behavior instead of hiding its NaNs.

`released-tokens.json` freezes the unchanged decoder's outputs for every individual vocabulary ID (51,865 Whisper and 8,193 Parakeet) plus 600 deterministic combinations per model. The aggregate single-token digests include each ID and output-byte length before its text; combination hashes and character counts catch joined multibyte UTF-8, leading spaces, special tokens and Unicode word/space behavior. Vocabulary archives are unchanged model data with lossless gzip compression, not Python implementations. [Tokenizer notices](tokenizer-NOTICE.md) record their sources and licenses; keep these test fixtures out of installed packages.

`released-onnx-inference.json` freezes eight actual released CPU recognitions: Whisper English automatic/forced, Chinese automatic/forced and doubled English; Parakeet English automatic/forced and doubled English. The longer 30.1025-second input exercises real 25-second splitting and joined output. Native `mluva-asr-worker` matches every final text SHA/character count using genuine pinned native ONNX libraries and models. Each model remains loaded across requests, then input EOF reaps its process; `/proc` disappearance is checked. The first physical comparison rejected an incorrect Parakeet int64 target/length input; the corrected worker uses the model's actual int32 tensors and passes. The fixture also records the released provider metadata for later integration; this kernel test compares final text only.

`released-onnx-cuda-inference.json` freezes the same eight requests through the unchanged CUDA client, with separate released outputs and provider metadata. Its SHA-256 is `0d8123690db06179af02497e983237ca579d52200d5d390dbda00cc530b86fd8`. Both released workers had independently observed NVIDIA compute contexts. Native workers match every final text SHA/character count on the physical RTX A1000 Laptop GPU. An external `nvidia-smi` observation also finds each owned native worker PID with nonzero allocated GPU memory; selecting a device flag alone cannot pass this check. All model processes are reaped after EOF. These are kernel results; parent metadata/errors and cancellation still need integration acceptance.

Both ignored physical tests were explicitly executed successfully. They require `MLUVA_ONNX_ASSETS` pointing to a separately prepared public asset store with `native-runtime/xdg-data/mluva/onnx-runtime/cpu/lib/`, `native-runtime/xdg-data/mluva/gpu-runtime/` and per-model `<id>/xdg-data/mluva/models/<id>-<revision-prefix>/` directories. The native production installer prepared both runtime stores and both model stores. Before inference, the checks independently verify every required model/native-library size and SHA and copy only those artifacts into disposable owner-only storage. The CUDA check additionally verifies all 34 installed native libraries/notices and the absence of other runtime files. Input PCM comes from frozen public fixtures and is WAV-encoded natively. Source collection uses a read-only host view with writable task-owned storage; native shader caches are private. No installed cache is used for inference or changed; no microphone, cloud inference, provider account, credentials or desktop input is used.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p mluva-asr
cargo test --locked -p mluva-asr --test inference \
  actual_cpu_whisper_and_parakeet_match_released_recognition \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p mluva-asr --test inference \
  actual_cuda_whisper_and_parakeet_match_released_recognition \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
```

This is same-machine/component evidence on an i7-12700H, not complete local-speech or application acceptance. [Native ONNX provisioning evidence](../../../mluva-providers/tests/fixtures/onnx-runtime-evidence.md) covers artifact installation and its cleanup. Broader languages/audio, empty/malformed WAV process behavior, loading/inference cancellation, parent-crash signaling, elapsed deadlines/RSS overflow, parent metadata/errors/session ownership, controller/UI/Live integration and final distribution remain required. The worker sets the CPU 5 GB address-space limit and a parent-death signal; those declarations alone are not independent fault acceptance. The installed app/widget remain v1.6.0, Python removal is pending and no performance improvement is claimed from debug-mode component checks or single GPU-memory observations.
